current_hypothesis: Any affine symplectic transvection fold that still preserves a symplectic 2-plane slice, even after an arbitrary common linear symplectic left factor, is blocked by the slice-area bound `R >= delta^(-1/2) >= 1`; the next live model must destroy every invariant symplectic slice rather than merely mixing it afterwards.
stop_reason: Attempt 015 implemented `src/transvection_fold_slice_obstruction.py`, verified the affine transvection and normalized fold formulas, ran a 5776-case nontrivial grid search over `(s,d,lambda)`, and audited 16 random common symplectic left factors. The best nontrivial slice radius was `1.001083448194763` at `(1.0, 0.9, -0.125)`, the identity baseline saturates the exact bound at `1.0`, all refined best cases have `s = 1.0`, and mixed left factors force the sharper bound `R >= delta^(-1/2)` with sampled lower bounds from `1.0083706647215258` to `2.1715166455758785` and observed radii from `1.4699275946793848` to `5.4926183121255905`. Therefore the entire slice-preserving/common-left-factor affine transvection-fold family is obstructed.

last_summary.worked: Implemented `src/transvection_fold_slice_obstruction.py`, a new audit for affine hyperplane folds generated by one-sided symplectic transvections. The script proves the preserved-slice area claim `R >= delta^(-1/2) >= 1`, runs a 5776-case nontrivial grid search over normalized folds, and audits 16 random common symplectic left factors. The saved report is `results/research_loop/attempt_015_transvection_fold_slice_obstruction.json`. The best nontrivial refined slice radius is `1.001083448194763` at `(s,d,lambda) = (1.0, 0.9, -0.125)`, while the identity baseline saturates the sharp lower bound at `1.0`.
last_summary.did_not_work: This more flexible transvection-fold family still does not make the proposed solution correct. The central active slice survives every normalized fold and every common symplectic left factor as a planar set of symplectic area `pi`, so no member of the family can compress below radius `1`, and generic mixing only makes the obstruction worse by decreasing `delta = |omega(f1,f2)|`. A naive attempt to extend the same area-`pi` argument to arbitrary linear pre-factors failed numerically, so pre-mixing remains unresolved rather than ruled out.
last_summary.next_step: Leave slice-preserving/common-left-factor affine transvection folds. The next live family should target pre-mixing before the fold or a genuinely nonlinear multi-stage local model, since those are the remaining ways to destroy or shrink the preserved-slice mechanism.
